title: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

intro.text: This entry describes intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA), a neurodevelopmental disorder whose causal gene I cannot reliably recall.

checks.claim: Intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is a neurodevelopmental disorder.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract (only text supplied) discusses autosomal recessive intellectual disability in general across 404 families. It does not name or describe IDPOGSA.

paragraphs.text: Intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is a neurodevelopmental disorder. Its cardinal features are impaired intellectual development and poor growth. Some patients also have seizures and/or ataxia.

checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. IDPOGSA is not mentioned in the abstract. The abstract only reports AR-ID genes in general terms.

checks.claim: Impaired intellectual development is a cardinal feature of IDPOGSA.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. The abstract is about intellectual disability as a whole and does not describe the features of IDPOGSA in particular. Any specific phenotype details would be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: Poor growth is a cardinal feature of IDPOGSA.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. Poor growth is not mentioned in the abstract. Phenotype details would only be in the full text, which was not supplied.

checks.claim: Some patients with IDPOGSA have seizures.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 3 cited papers. Seizures are not mentioned in the abstract. The full text was not supplied.

checks.claim: Some patients with IDPOGSA have ataxia.
checks.evidence_quote: Symptoms of the two affected subjects were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.explanation: The paper describes ataxia in two siblings with an ABCA2 variant. It does not name IDPOGSA or describe ataxia as occurring in only some patients.
